Firing continuous rapid strings with little to no cool down period will “wreck” a barrel, but even that is subjective, depending on your needs.

For example, if you are a bench rest shooter shooting handloaded 6mm at max velocities, you may experience a drop off in accuracy in as little as 1k rounds. Going from .3 to .6 MOA may lose you a match, but if you aren’t shooting matches, then this may not matter to you at all.

If you are a hunter shooting .308 Winchester with a preferred factory loaded hot and you go from .8 to 1.5 MOA, your deflection at hunting ranges is still going to be in the vitals.

If you are shooting 6.5 CM at 500-1000 yds and begin to suffer some loss in accuracy after 3k rounds of measured 3 to 5 round groups with moderate cool down intervals, I’d say you used the hell out of that gun on many trips and should probably rebarrel or chop it down and rechamber.

Either way, you win
